protections: P1: stored prompt templates are rendered in a sandboxed template engine so that template expressions cannot reach Python object internals (missing at render time: plain jinja2 Environment at mcpgateway/services/prompt_service.py:88, used by _compile_jinja_template at prompt_service.py:96-106 and _render_template at prompt_service.py:2887-2889).

P2 (weak, pre-existing): write-time blocklist on template text via SecurityValidator.validate_template (mcpgateway/common/validators.py:841-876), wired as a pydantic field validator on PromptCreate/PromptUpdate (mcpgateway/schemas.py:2432-2443, mcpgateway/schemas.py:2602-2611).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: A write-time SSTI blocklist already runs on every PromptCreate/PromptUpdate (validators.py:841-876, schemas.py:2432-2443), so render-time sandboxing looks redundant.
The str.format fallback looks like legacy {name}-style compatibility, not the Jinja sink the report names.

Federated prompts are treated as upstream-fetched metadata (prompt_service.py:340-354, 2004-2007); also their data already passes PromptCreate.model_validate (gateway_service.py:5508), so the schema blocklist does run.
Separate plugin package rendering operator-configured payload templates, far from prompt_service.

masking: T2 only matters once T1 is fixed: with a sandbox in place, a sandbox rejection is caught by the bare except at prompt_service.py:2890 and the raw template is re-rendered via str.format at prompt_service.py:2892.

conflicts.what: Fixing T1 by tightening the write-time blocklist (validators.py:97-135) instead of sandboxing rejects ordinary templates; the existing list already rejects common characters inside {{ }} expressions, so more tokens break ordinary prompts.
Removing the str.format fallback outright breaks {name}-style templates, which _get_required_arguments still treats as first-class (prompt_service.py:2861-2863).

fairness_risks: Plain Jinja templates with variables and control blocks must keep rendering (prompt_service.py:2881-2885, validators.py:758-763); hidden tests must not require refusing them.

{name}-style templates are supported via the format fallback (prompt_service.py:2861-2863, 2892); a test that requires removing the fallback entirely contradicts that behaviour. Tests should only require that sandbox rejections do not fall through.
Rendering is skipped when no arguments are given (prompt_service.py:2008-2017), so behavioural tests must pass arguments to reach the sink.

design.why: As found, the natural code gives only two independent holes (T1 render env with T4 folded into it, and T2 fallback) plus one coupled constraint (T3). That is short of 3-5 independent traps unless T5 is injected. If injection is allowed, T1 (landing point) + T2 (deepseek-type: legacy-fallback dismissal, masked until T1 is fixed) + T3 (mimo-type: ordinary templates must keep rendering, so no over-hardening) + injected T5 (separate plugin render site) gives four judgements with different dismissal reasons. T4 is not independent: the render-time sandbox closes it, and the schema blocklist already runs on federated data (gateway_service.py:5508).

unverified: Relationship of pinned commit 0f8e0ad6 to fix commit 4d31004 not checked in git; the code at the pin is consistent with pre-fix state (plain Environment at prompt_service.py:88).
Whether mcp.types.Prompt carries a 'template' field through model_dump (gateway_service.py:5503-5506); if not, federated templates are always empty and T4 is unreachable.
The objects assigned at gateway_service.py:4818/1258 were assumed to be the PromptCreate list built at gateway_service.py:5508; not traced end to end.
How strong the existing write-time blocklist (validators.py:97-135, 841-876) is was deliberately not probed. Whether it fully closes T1 before a sandbox is added is not assessed here.
Whether the str.format fallback (prompt_service.py:2892) exposes anything beyond reprs with Dict[str,str] arguments.
T5 injection site: only the function signature and call (webhook_notification.py:146, 228) were seen; its body and the code comment about Jinja2 cited by the screener were not read.
resource_service.py:3698-3704 injection room cited by the screener was not read.
Admin add/edit routes (admin.py) were assumed to build PromptCreate/PromptUpdate; not read.

Other jinja2 Environments (main.py:3309, version.py:1536, email_notification_service.py:37, tools/builder/common.py) load file-system templates and were judged out of scope without reading their sources of template text.
